paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the empirical generalization errors on the BoolQ dataset across different rank values. The x-axis is labeled "Rank" and utilizes a logarithmic scale with tick labels plotted at 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis, representing errors as indicated by the title, uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 0.6 with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The plot features a single solid black line with large green circular markers and capped vertical black error bars at each plotted data point. The line begins at an x-value of 4 with a y-value of approximately 0.27. It then exhibits a slight decline to its lowest point at an x-value of 16, where the y-value is roughly 0.24. Following this minimum, the line steadily increases, reaching a y-value of approximately 0.30 at an x-value of 64, and concludes at its peak of roughly 0.35 at the final x-value of 256.
